# Subagent-Driven Development

Execute plan by dispatching fresh subagent per task, with two-stage review after each: spec compliance review first, then code quality review.

**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review (spec then quality) = high quality, fast iteration

## When to Use

```dot
digraph when_to_use {
    "Have implementation plan?" [shape=diamond];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" [shape=diamond];
    "Stay in this session?" [shape=diamond];
    "subagent-driven-development" [shape=box];
    "executing-plans" [shape=box];
    "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [shape=box];

    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Tasks mostly independent?" [label="yes"];
    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Stay in this session?" [label="yes"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no - tightly coupled"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "subagent-driven-development" [label="yes"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "executing-plans" [label="no - parallel session"];
}
```

**vs. Executing Plans (parallel session):**
- Same session (no context switch)
- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution)
- Two-stage review after each task: spec compliance first, then code quality
- Faster iteration (no human-in-loop between tasks)

## The Process

```dot
digraph process {
    rankdir=TB;

    subgraph cluster_per_task {
        label="Per Task";
        "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];
        "Implementer subagent asks questions?" [shape=diamond];
        "Answer questions, provide context" [shape=box];
        "Implementer subagent implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" [shape=box];
        "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];
        "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" [shape=diamond];
        "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" [shape=box];
        "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];
        "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?" [shape=diamond];
        "Implementer subagent fixes quality issues" [shape=box];
        "Mark task complete in TodoWrite" [shape=box];
    }

    "Read plan, extract all tasks with full text, note context, create TodoWrite" [shape=box];
    "More tasks remain?" [shape=diamond];
    "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" [shape=box];
    "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch" [shape=box style=filled fillcolor=lightgreen];

    "Read plan, extract all tasks with full text, note context, create TodoWrite" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)";
    "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" -> "Implementer subagent asks questions?";
    "Implementer subagent asks questions?" -> "Answer questions, provide context" [label="yes"];
    "Answer questions, provide context" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)";
    "Implementer subagent asks questions?" -> "Implementer subagent implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" [label="no"];
    "Implementer subagent implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" -> "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)";
    "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" -> "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?";
    "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" -> "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" [label="no"];
    "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" -> "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="re-review"];
    "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" -> "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="yes"];
    "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" -> "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?";
    "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?" -> "Implementer subagent fixes quality issues" [label="no"];
    "Implementer subagent fixes quality issues" -> "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="re-review"];
    "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?" -> "Mark task complete in TodoWrite" [label="yes"];
    "Mark task complete in TodoWrite" -> "More tasks remain?";
    "More tasks remain?" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" [label="yes"];
    "More tasks remain?" -> "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" [label="no"];
    "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" -> "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch";
}
```

## Prompt Templates

- `./implementer-prompt.md` - Dispatch implementer subagent
- `./spec-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch spec compliance reviewer subagent
- `./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent

## Example Workflow

```
You: I'm using Subagent-Driven Development to execute this plan.

[Read plan file once: docs/plans/feature-plan.md]
[Extract all 5 tasks with full text and context]
[Create TodoWrite with all tasks]

Task 1: Hook installation script

[Get Task 1 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: "Before I begin - should the hook be installed at user or system level?"

You: "User level (~/.config/superpowers/hooks/)"

Implementer: "Got it. Implementing now..."
[Later] Implementer:
  - Implemented install-hook command
  - Added tests, 5/5 passing
  - Self-review: Found I missed --force flag, added it
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]
Spec reviewer: ✅ Spec compliant - all requirements met, nothing extra

[Get git SHAs, dispatch code quality reviewer]
Code reviewer: Strengths: Good test coverage, clean. Issues: None. Approved.

[Mark Task 1 complete]

Task 2: Recovery modes

[Get Task 2 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: [No questions, proceeds]
Implementer:
  - Added verify/repair modes
  - 8/8 tests passing
  - Self-review: All good
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]
Spec reviewer: ❌ Issues:
  - Missing: Progress reporting (spec says "report every 100 items")
  - Extra: Added --json flag (not requested)

[Implementer fixes issues]
Implementer: Removed --json flag, added progress reporting

[Spec reviewer reviews again]
Spec reviewer: ✅ Spec compliant now

[Dispatch code quality reviewer]
Code reviewer: Strengths: Solid. Issues (Important): Magic number (100)

[Implementer fixes]
Implementer: Extracted PROGRESS_INTERVAL constant

[Code reviewer reviews again]
Code reviewer: ✅ Approved

[Mark Task 2 complete]

...

[After all tasks]
[Dispatch final code-reviewer]
Final reviewer: All requirements met, ready to merge

Done!
```

## Advantages

**vs. Manual execution:**
- Subagents follow TDD naturally
- Fresh context per task (no confusion)
- Parallel-safe (subagents don't interfere)
- Subagent can ask questions (before AND during work)

**vs. Executing Plans:**
- Same session (no handoff)
- Continuous progress (no waiting)
- Review checkpoints automatic

**Efficiency gains:**
- No file reading overhead (controller provides full text)
- Controller curates exactly what context is needed
- Subagent gets complete information upfront
- Questions surfaced before work begins (not after)

**Quality gates:**
- Self-review catches issues before handoff
- Two-stage review: spec compliance, then code quality
- Review loops ensure fixes actually work
- Spec compliance prevents over/under-building
- Code quality ensures implementation is well-built

**Cost:**
- More subagent invocations (implementer + 2 reviewers per task)
- Controller does more prep work (extracting all tasks upfront)
- Review loops add iterations
- But catches issues early (cheaper than debugging later)

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent
- Skip reviews (spec compliance OR code quality)
- Proceed with unfixed issues
- Dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel (conflicts)
- Make subagent read plan file (provide full text instead)
- Skip scene-setting context (subagent needs to understand where task fits)
- Ignore subagent questions (answer before letting them proceed)
- Accept "close enough" on spec compliance (spec reviewer found issues = not done)
- Skip review loops (reviewer found issues = implementer fixes = review again)
- Let implementer self-review replace actual review (both are needed)
- **Start code quality review before spec compliance is ✅** (wrong order)
- Move to next task while either review has open issues

**If subagent asks questions:**
- Answer clearly and completely
- Provide additional context if needed
- Don't rush them into implementation

**If reviewer finds issues:**
- Implementer (same subagent) fixes them
- Reviewer reviews again
- Repeat until approved
- Don't skip the re-review

**If subagent fails task:**
- Dispatch fix subagent with specific instructions
- Don't try to fix manually (context pollution)

## Integration

**Required workflow skills:**
- **superpowers:using-git-worktrees** - REQUIRED: Set up isolated workspace before starting
- **superpowers:writing-plans** - Creates the plan this skill executes
- **superpowers:requesting-code-review** - Code review template for reviewer subagents
- **superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch** - Complete development after all tasks

**Subagents should use:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - Subagents follow TDD for each task

**Alternative workflow:**
- **superpowers:executing-plans** - Use for parallel session instead of same-session execution

# Implementer Subagent Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching an implementer subagent.

```
Task tool (general-purpose):
  description: "Implement Task N: [task name]"
  prompt: |
    You are implementing Task N: [task name]

    ## Task Description

    [FULL TEXT of task from plan - paste it here, don't make subagent read file]

    ## Context

    [Scene-setting: where this fits, dependencies, architectural context]

    ## Before You Begin

    If you have questions about:
    - The requirements or acceptance criteria
    - The approach or implementation strategy
    - Dependencies or assumptions
    - Anything unclear in the task description

    **Ask them now.** Raise any concerns before starting work.

    ## Your Job

    Once you're clear on requirements:
    1. Implement exactly what the task specifies
    2. Write tests (following TDD if task says to)
    3. Verify implementation works
    4. Commit your work
    5. Self-review (see below)
    6. Report back

    Work from: [directory]

    **While you work:** If you encounter something unexpected or unclear, **ask questions**.
    It's always OK to pause and clarify. Don't guess or make assumptions.

    ## Before Reporting Back: Self-Review

    Review your work with fresh eyes. Ask yourself:

    **Completeness:**
    - Did I fully implement everything in the spec?
    - Did I miss any requirements?
    - Are there edge cases I didn't handle?

    **Quality:**
    - Is this my best work?
    - Are names clear and accurate (match what things do, not how they work)?
    - Is the code clean and maintainable?

    **Discipline:**
    - Did I avoid overbuilding (YAGNI)?
    - Did I only build what was requested?
    - Did I follow existing patterns in the codebase?

    **Testing:**
    - Do tests actually verify behavior (not just mock behavior)?
    - Did I follow TDD if required?
    - Are tests comprehensive?

    If you find issues during self-review, fix them now before reporting.

    ## Report Format

    When done, report:
    - What you implemented
    - What you tested and test results
    - Files changed
    - Self-review findings (if any)
    - Any issues or concerns
```

# Spec Compliance Reviewer Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching a spec compliance reviewer subagent.

**Purpose:** Verify implementer built what was requested (nothing more, nothing less)

```
Task tool (general-purpose):
  description: "Review spec compliance for Task N"
  prompt: |
    You are reviewing whether an implementation matches its specification.

    ## What Was Requested

    [FULL TEXT of task requirements]

    ## What Implementer Claims They Built

    [From implementer's report]

    ## CRITICAL: Do Not Trust the Report

    The implementer finished suspiciously quickly. Their report may be incomplete,
    inaccurate, or optimistic. You MUST verify everything independently.

    **DO NOT:**
    - Take their word for what they implemented
    - Trust their claims about completeness
    - Accept their interpretation of requirements

    **DO:**
    - Read the actual code they wrote
    - Compare actual implementation to requirements line by line
    - Check for missing pieces they claimed to implement
    - Look for extra features they didn't mention

    ## Your Job

    Read the implementation code and verify:

    **Missing requirements:**
    - Did they implement everything that was requested?
    - Are there requirements they skipped or missed?
    - Did they claim something works but didn't actually implement it?

    **Extra/unneeded work:**
    - Did they build things that weren't requested?
    - Did they over-engineer or add unnecessary features?
    - Did they add "nice to haves" that weren't in spec?

    **Misunderstandings:**
    - Did they interpret requirements differently than intended?
    - Did they solve the wrong problem?
    - Did they implement the right feature but wrong way?

    **Verify by reading code, not by trusting report.**

    Report:
    - ✅ Spec compliant (if everything matches after code inspection)
    - ❌ Issues found: [list specifically what's missing or extra, with file:line references]
```

**Files:**

**Step 1: Add litellm to pyproject.toml**

In `backend/pyproject.toml`, add `litellm` to the `[tool.poetry.dependencies]` section. Add this line after the `docker` dependency:

litellm = "^1.72.0"
```

**Step 2: Install dependency**

git add backend/pyproject.toml backend/poetry.lock
git commit -m "feat(gateway): add litellm dependency for multi-provider support"
```

This is the first task in implementing the Claude Gateway — a LiteLLM-based translation layer that lets the app use non-Anthropic models (OpenAI, Gemini, Mistral, etc.). We're adding litellm as a dependency first before writing any code.

IMPORTANT: Use `poetry lock` and `poetry install` (not poetry add) since we're editing pyproject.toml directly. The commands may need sandbox disabled for file system access.

"""
Claude Gateway: LiteLLM-based translation layer for non-Anthropic models.

Routes non-Anthropic model requests through LiteLLM, translating between
the Anthropic Messages API format and each provider's native format.
"""

import json
import uuid

import litellm

_ANTHROPIC_SHORT_ALIASES = {"haiku", "sonnet", "opus"}


def is_anthropic_model(model: str) -> bool:
    """Return True if model name refers to an Anthropic Claude model."""
    if not model:
        return True
    name = model.lower().strip()
    if name.startswith("claude"):
        return True
    if name in _ANTHROPIC_SHORT_ALIASES:
        return True
    return False

1→"""
     2→Claude Gateway: LiteLLM-based translation layer for non-Anthropic models.
     3→
     4→Routes non-Anthropic model requests through LiteLLM, translating between
     5→the Anthropic Messages API format and each provider's native format.
     6→"""
     7→
     8→import json
     9→import uuid
    10→
    11→import litellm
    12→
    13→_ANTHROPIC_SHORT_ALIASES = {"haiku", "sonnet", "opus"}
    14→
    15→
    16→def is_anthropic_model(model: str) -> bool:
    17→    """Return True if model name refers to an Anthropic Claude model."""
    18→    if not model:
    19→        return True
    20→    name = model.lower().strip()
    21→    if name.startswith("claude"):
    22→        return True
    23→    if name in _ANTHROPIC_SHORT_ALIASES:
    24→        return True
    25→    return False
    26→
    27→
    28→def _convert_system_to_openai(system) -> str:
    29→    if isinstance(system, str):
    30→        return system
    31→    if isinstance(system, list):
    32→        return "\n".join(block.get("text", "") for block in system if block.get("type") == "text")
    33→    return str(system)
    34→
    35→
    36→def _convert_message_to_openai(msg: dict) -> list[dict]:
    37→    role = msg.get("role", "user")
    38→    content = msg.get("content", "")
    39→
    40→    if isinstance(content, str):
    41→        return [{"role": role, "content": content}]
    42→
    43→    if isinstance(content, list):
    44→        tool_results = [b for b in content if b.get("type") == "tool_result"]
    45→        if tool_results:
    46→            result_msgs = []
    47→            for tr in tool_results:
    48→                tr_content = tr.get("content", "")
    49→                if isinstance(tr_content, list):
    50→                    tr_content = "\n".join(
    51→                        b.get("text", "") for b in tr_content if b.get("type") == "text"
    52→                    )
    53→                result_msgs.append({
    54→                    "role": "tool",
    55→                    "tool_call_id": tr["tool_use_id"],
    56→                    "content": str(tr_content),
    57→                })
    58→            return result_msgs
    59→
    60→        tool_uses = [b for b in content if b.get("type") == "tool_use"]
    61→        text_blocks = [b for b in content if b.get("type") == "text"]
    62→        text_content = "\n".join(b.get("text", "") for b in text_blocks) if text_blocks else None
    63→
    64→        if tool_uses:
    65→            openai_msg: dict = {"role": "assistant", "content": text_content}
    66→            openai_msg["tool_calls"] = [
    67→                {
    68→                    "id": tu["id"],
    69→                    "type": "function",
    70→                    "function": {
    71→                        "name": tu["name"],
    72→                        "arguments": json.dumps(tu["input"]),
    73→                    },
    74→                }
    75→                for tu in tool_uses
    76→            ]
    77→            return [openai_msg]
    78→
    79→        combined = "\n".join(b.get("text", "") for b in content if b.get("type") == "text")
    80→        return [{"role": role, "content": combined}]
    81→
    82→    return [{"role": role, "content": str(content)}]
    83→
    84→
    85→def translate_request_to_openai(anthropic_body: dict) -> dict:
    86→    openai_messages: list[dict] = []
    87→
    88→    system = anthropic_body.get("system")
    89→    if system:
    90→        openai_messages.append({
    91→            "role": "system",
    92→            "content": _convert_system_to_openai(system),
    93→        })
    94→
    95→    for msg in anthropic_body.get("messages", []):
    96→        openai_messages.extend(_convert_message_to_openai(msg))
    97→
    98→    result: dict = {
    99→        "model": anthropic_body["model"],
   100→        "messages": openai_messages,
   101→    }
   102→
   103→    if "max_tokens" in anthropic_body:
   104→        result["max_tokens"] = anthropic_body["max_tokens"]
   105→
   106→    tools = anthropic_body.get("tools")
   107→    if tools:
   108→        result["tools"] = [
   109→            {
   110→                "type": "function",
   111→                "function": {
   112→                    "name": t["name"],
   113→                    "description": t.get("description", ""),
   114→                    "parameters": t.get("input_schema", {}),
   115→                },
   116→            }
   117→            for t in tools
   118→        ]
   119→
   120→    return result
   121→
   122→
   123→_FINISH_REASON_MAP = {
   124→    "stop": "end_turn",
   125→    "length": "max_tokens",
   126→    "tool_calls": "tool_use",
   127→    "content_filter": "end_turn",
   128→}
   129→
   130→
   131→def translate_response_to_anthropic(openai_resp: dict, model: str) -> dict:
   132→    choice = openai_resp["choices"][0]
   133→    message = choice["message"]
   134→    finish_reason = choice.get("finish_reason", "stop")
   135→
   136→    content_blocks: list[dict] = []
   137→
   138→    text = message.get("content")
   139→    if text:
   140→        content_blocks.append({"type": "text", "text": text})
   141→
   142→    tool_calls = message.get("tool_calls", [])
   143→    for tc in tool_calls:
   144→        func = tc["function"]
   145→        try:
   146→            input_data = json.loads(func["arguments"])
   147→        except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
   148→            input_data = {"raw": func.get("arguments", "")}
   149→        content_blocks.append({
   150→            "type": "tool_use",
   151→            "id": tc["id"],
   152→            "name": func["name"],
   153→            "input": input_data,
   154→        })
   155→
   156→    usage = openai_resp.get("usage", {})
   157→
   158→    return {
   159→        "id": f"msg_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:24]}",
   160→        "type": "message",
   161→        "role": "assistant",
   162→        "model": model,
   163→        "content": content_blocks if content_blocks else [{"type": "text", "text": ""}],
   164→        "stop_reason": _FINISH_REASON_MAP.get(finish_reason, "end_turn"),
   165→        "stop_sequence": None,
   166→        "usage": {
   167→            "input_tokens": usage.get("prompt_tokens", 0),
   168→            "output_tokens": usage.get("completion_tokens", 0),
   169→        },
   170→    }
   171→

1→"""
     2→Claude Gateway: LiteLLM-based translation layer for non-Anthropic models.
     3→
     4→Routes non-Anthropic model requests through LiteLLM, translating between
     5→the Anthropic Messages API format and each provider's native format.
     6→"""
     7→
     8→import json
     9→import uuid
    10→
    11→import litellm
    12→
    13→_ANTHROPIC_SHORT_ALIASES = {"haiku", "sonnet", "opus"}
    14→
    15→
    16→def is_anthropic_model(model: str) -> bool:
    17→    """Return True if model name refers to an Anthropic Claude model."""
    18→    if not model:
    19→        return True
    20→    name = model.lower().strip()
    21→    if name.startswith("claude-") or name == "claude":
    22→        return True
    23→    if name in _ANTHROPIC_SHORT_ALIASES:
    24→        return True
    25→    return False
    26→
    27→
    28→def _convert_system_to_openai(system) -> str:
    29→    if isinstance(system, str):
    30→        return system
    31→    if isinstance(system, list):
    32→        return "\n".join(block.get("text", "") for block in system if block.get("type") == "text")
    33→    return str(system)
    34→
    35→
    36→def _convert_message_to_openai(msg: dict) -> list[dict]:
    37→    role = msg.get("role", "user")
    38→    content = msg.get("content", "")
    39→
    40→    if isinstance(content, str):
    41→        return [{"role": role, "content": content}]
    42→
    43→    if isinstance(content, list):
    44→        tool_results = [b for b in content if b.get("type") == "tool_result"]
    45→        if tool_results:
    46→            result_msgs = []
    47→            for tr in tool_results:
    48→                tr_content = tr.get("content", "")
    49→                if isinstance(tr_content, list):
    50→                    tr_content = "\n".join(
    51→                        b.get("text", "") for b in tr_content if b.get("type") == "text"
    52→                    )
    53→                result_msgs.append({
    54→                    "role": "tool",
    55→                    "tool_call_id": tr["tool_use_id"],
    56→                    "content": str(tr_content),
    57→                })
    58→            return result_msgs
    59→
    60→        tool_uses = [b for b in content if b.get("type") == "tool_use"]
    61→        text_blocks = [b for b in content if b.get("type") == "text"]
    62→        text_content = "\n".join(b.get("text", "") for b in text_blocks) if text_blocks else None
    63→
    64→        if tool_uses:
    65→            openai_msg: dict = {"role": "assistant", "content": text_content}
    66→            openai_msg["tool_calls"] = [
    67→                {
    68→                    "id": tu["id"],
    69→                    "type": "function",
    70→                    "function": {
    71→                        "name": tu["name"],
    72→                        "arguments": json.dumps(tu["input"]),
    73→                    },
    74→                }
    75→                for tu in tool_uses
    76→            ]
    77→            return [openai_msg]
    78→
    79→        combined = "\n".join(b.get("text", "") for b in content if b.get("type") == "text")
    80→        return [{"role": role, "content": combined}]
    81→
    82→    return [{"role": role, "content": str(content)}]
    83→
    84→
    85→def translate_request_to_openai(anthropic_body: dict) -> dict:
    86→    openai_messages: list[dict] = []
    87→
    88→    system = anthropic_body.get("system")
    89→    if system:
    90→        openai_messages.append({
    91→            "role": "system",
    92→            "content": _convert_system_to_openai(system),
    93→        })
    94→
    95→    for msg in anthropic_body.get("messages", []):
    96→        openai_messages.extend(_convert_message_to_openai(msg))
    97→
    98→    result: dict = {
    99→        "model": anthropic_body["model"],
   100→        "messages": openai_messages,
   101→    }
   102→
   103→    if "max_tokens" in anthropic_body:
   104→        result["max_tokens"] = anthropic_body["max_tokens"]
   105→
   106→    tools = anthropic_body.get("tools")
   107→    if tools:
   108→        result["tools"] = [
   109→            {
   110→                "type": "function",
   111→                "function": {
   112→                    "name": t["name"],
   113→                    "description": t.get("description", ""),
   114→                    "parameters": t.get("input_schema", {}),
   115→                },
   116→            }
   117→            for t in tools
   118→        ]
   119→
   120→    return result
   121→
   122→
   123→_FINISH_REASON_MAP = {
   124→    "stop": "end_turn",
   125→    "length": "max_tokens",
   126→    "tool_calls": "tool_use",
   127→    "content_filter": "end_turn",
   128→}
   129→
   130→
   131→def translate_response_to_anthropic(openai_resp: dict, model: str) -> dict:
   132→    choice = openai_resp["choices"][0]
   133→    message = choice["message"]
   134→    finish_reason = choice.get("finish_reason", "stop")
   135→
   136→    content_blocks: list[dict] = []
   137→
   138→    text = message.get("content")
   139→    if text:
   140→        content_blocks.append({"type": "text", "text": text})
   141→
   142→    tool_calls = message.get("tool_calls", [])
   143→    for tc in tool_calls:
   144→        func = tc["function"]
   145→        try:
   146→            input_data = json.loads(func["arguments"])
   147→        except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
   148→            input_data = {"raw": func.get("arguments", "")}
   149→        content_blocks.append({
   150→            "type": "tool_use",
   151→            "id": tc["id"],
   152→            "name": func["name"],
   153→            "input": input_data,
   154→        })
   155→
   156→    usage = openai_resp.get("usage", {})
   157→
   158→    return {
   159→        "id": f"msg_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:24]}",
   160→        "type": "message",
   161→        "role": "assistant",
   162→        "model": model,
   163→        "content": content_blocks if content_blocks else [{"type": "text", "text": ""}],
   164→        "stop_reason": _FINISH_REASON_MAP.get(finish_reason, "end_turn"),
   165→        "stop_sequence": None,
   166→        "usage": {
   167→            "input_tokens": usage.get("prompt_tokens", 0),
   168→            "output_tokens": usage.get("completion_tokens", 0),
   169→        },
   170→    }
   171→

content.content:
# Claude Gateway: Multi-Provider Model Support via LiteLLM

**Date:** 2026-02-26
**Status:** Approved

## Problem

The application is locked to Anthropic models. Users who want to use OpenAI, Google Gemini, Mistral, or other providers must wait for native support or switch tools entirely.

## Solution

Embed a LiteLLM-based translation layer in the existing credential proxy (`proxy.py`). When the Claude Agent SDK makes API calls through the proxy, the gateway detects whether the target model is Anthropic or non-Anthropic and routes accordingly:

- **Anthropic models** -> forward to `api.anthropic.com` (existing behavior, unchanged)
- **Non-Anthropic models** -> use LiteLLM to translate the Anthropic Messages API request to the target provider's format, call the provider, and translate the response back to Anthropic format

The sidecar, Claude Agent SDK, frontend, and agent logic remain completely untouched.

```
SDK -> POST /anthropic/v1/messages -> proxy.py
  |-- model=claude-* -> forward to api.anthropic.com (existing)
  |-- model=gpt-4o   -> gateway.py -> LiteLLM -> openai.com -> translate response -> Anthropic format
```

## Architecture

### Model Detection & Routing

A helper function `is_anthropic_model(model_name)` classifies model names:

- **Anthropic:** `claude-*`, plus short aliases `haiku`, `sonnet`, `opus`
- **Non-Anthropic:** everything else, using LiteLLM's naming convention (`gpt-4o`, `gemini/gemini-2.0-flash`, `mistral/mistral-large-latest`, `ollama/llama3`, etc.)

Routing in `proxy.py` intercepts `POST` requests to `v1/messages`. All other paths forward to Anthropic as before, except `GET v1/models` which is augmented (see below).

```python
# In proxy_anthropic(), simplified:
if method == "POST" and path == "v1/messages":
    body = parse_json(request)
    model = body.get("model", "")
    if not is_anthropic_model(model):
        return await gateway_handler(body, stream=body.get("stream", False))
# Otherwise fall through to existing upstream forwarding
```

### Model Alias Resolution (`/v1/models`)

The Claude Agent SDK calls `GET /v1/models` to resolve short aliases (e.g., `haiku` -> `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`) for both orchestrator and subagent models. Non-Anthropic model names would fail this resolution.

Solution: always intercept `GET /v1/models`:

1. Forward to `api.anthropic.com` to get real Anthropic models
2. Collect all configured non-Anthropic model names from env vars (`ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, `SQL_SUBAGENT_MODEL`, `CHART_SUBAGENT_MODEL`)
3. Append synthetic entries for non-Anthropic models so the SDK's alias resolution accepts them

This enables mixed-provider configurations:
```bash
ANTHROPIC_MODEL=gpt-4o                        # orchestrator on OpenAI
SQL_SUBAGENT_MODEL=haiku                       # subagent on Anthropic
REDACTED.0-flash   # subagent on Google
```

### Request/Response Translation (`gateway.py`)

New module `backend/app/gateway.py` handles bidirectional translation using LiteLLM.

**Non-streaming flow:**

1. Receive Anthropic Messages API request body (`model`, `messages`, `system`, `tools`, `max_tokens`, etc.)
2. Convert to OpenAI-compatible format (LiteLLM's internal standard)
3. Call `litellm.acompletion(model="gpt-4o", messages=[...], tools=[...])`
4. Convert the OpenAI-format response back to Anthropic Messages API response (`content` blocks with `type: "text"` / `type: "tool_use"`, `stop_reason`, `usage`, etc.)
5. Return as JSON HTTP response

**Streaming flow:**

1. Same request translation
2. Call `litellm.acompletion(model="gpt-4o", ..., stream=True)`
3. Convert each OpenAI streaming chunk to Anthropic SSE events:
   - Emit `message_start` with message metadata
   - Convert `choices[].delta.content` -> `content_block_delta` with `text_delta`
   - Convert `choices[].delta.tool_calls` -> `content_block_start` + `content_block_delta` with `input_json_delta`
   - Emit `message_delta` with `stop_reason` and final `usage`
   - Emit `message_stop`
4. Yield as `text/event-stream` response

**Tool use round-trip (critical path):**

- **Request direction:** Anthropic `tools` array (name, description, input_schema) -> OpenAI `tools` array (function name, description, parameters). Straightforward mapping.
- **Response direction:** OpenAI `tool_calls` (function name, arguments as JSON string) -> Anthropic `tool_use` content blocks (name, input as parsed object, unique `id`).
- **Tool results:** Anthropic `tool_result` messages (with `tool_use_id`) -> OpenAI `tool` role messages. LiteLLM handles this natively.

### Configuration

**Existing env vars** get broader meaning -- they now accept any LiteLLM model name:

- `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` -- orchestrator model (default: `claude-sonnet-4-6`)
- `SQL_SUBAGENT_MODEL` -- sql analyst subagent (default: `haiku`)
- `CHART_SUBAGENT_MODEL` -- chart builder subagent (default: `haiku`)

**New env vars** for provider API keys (LiteLLM reads these automatically from the environment):

- `OPENAI_API_KEY` -- for GPT models
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` -- for Google Gemini
- `MISTRAL_API_KEY` -- for Mistral
- `GROQ_API_KEY` -- for Groq
- Any other provider key supported by LiteLLM

`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` warning in `config.py` is relaxed -- it's no longer required if using only non-Anthropic providers.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `backend/app/gateway.py` | **New** -- LiteLLM translation layer (~250 lines) |
| `backend/app/proxy.py` | Modify routing to detect non-Anthropic models and delegate to gateway; augment `/v1/models` response |
| `backend/app/config.py` | Relax `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` warning |
| `backend/.env.example` | Add provider key examples and non-Anthropic model examples |
| `backend/pyproject.toml` | Add `litellm` dependency |

**No changes to:** sidecar, frontend, agent.py, container_manager, MCP tools.

## Limitations

- **Anthropic-specific features** (prompt caching, extended thinking, citations, PDF input) are silently dropped for non-Anthropic models
- **Tool use quality varies** across providers -- GPT-4o and Gemini handle multi-step tool chains well, smaller/open-source models may struggle
- **Streaming latency** -- adds one translation hop but no extra network round-trips
- **Provider-specific errors** need translation to Anthropic error format for the SDK to handle gracefully

1→import logging
     2→import uuid
     3→from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
     4→
     5→from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Request
     6→from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
     7→import httpx
     8→
     9→from app.config import ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
    10→
    11→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    12→
    13→ANTHROPIC_UPSTREAM = "https://api.anthropic.com"
    14→
    15→_SKIP_REQUEST_HEADERS = {
    16→    "host", "content-length", "transfer-encoding", "connection",
    17→    "x-api-key",         # client must not override billing identity
    18→    "anthropic-version", # proxy controls API version
    19→    # anthropic-beta is intentionally NOT blocked: Claude Code sends beta body
    20→    # fields (e.g. context_management) alongside the matching beta header, and
    21→    # Anthropic rejects those fields as "extra inputs" if the header is absent.
    22→}
    23→_SKIP_RESPONSE_HEADERS = {"transfer-encoding", "content-encoding", "connection"}
    24→
    25→
    26→class ProxyTokenStore:
    27→    def __init__(self, ttl_seconds: int = 600):
    28→        self._ttl = ttl_seconds
    29→        self._tokens: dict[str, datetime] = {}
    30→
    31→    def create_token(self) -> str:
    32→        token = str(uuid.uuid4())
    33→        self._tokens[token] = datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(seconds=self._ttl)
    34→        return token
    35→
    36→    def validate_token(self, token: str) -> bool:
    37→        # Tokens are intentionally multi-use: Claude Code makes many API calls
    38→        # per session, all protected by the same UUID. The token is valid for
    39→        # the session TTL (600s safety net) but is explicitly revoked by
    40→        # proxy_token_store.revoke_token() in agent.py's finally block when
    41→        # the Claude Code subprocess exits. Do not make single-use.
    42→        expiry = self._tokens.get(token)
    43→        if expiry is None:
    44→            return False
    45→        if datetime.now(timezone.utc) > expiry:
    46→            self._tokens.pop(token, None)
    47→            return False
    48→        return True
    49→
    50→    def revoke_token(self, token: str) -> None:
    51→        self._tokens.pop(token, None)
    52→
    53→    def cleanup_expired(self) -> int:
    54→        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    55→        expired = [t for t, exp in self._tokens.items() if now > exp]
    56→        for t in expired:
    57→            del self._tokens[t]
    58→        return len(expired)
    59→
    60→
    61→proxy_token_store = ProxyTokenStore()
    62→
    63→router = APIRouter(prefix="/anthropic")
    64→
    65→
    66→# Read-only discovery endpoints that the Claude Code SDK calls during startup
    67→# (e.g. GET /v1/models to resolve short model aliases like "sonnet").
    68→# These carry no session-specific data, so we forward them with the real API
    69→# key without requiring a registered session token.
    70→_UNAUTHENTICATED_PASSTHROUGH = {"v1/models"}
    71→
    72→
    73→@router.api_route("/{path:path}", methods=["GET", "POST", "PUT", "DELETE", "PATCH"])
    74→async def proxy_anthropic(path: str, request: Request):
    75→    # Allow a small set of read-only discovery endpoints to pass through
    76→    # without a session token so the SDK can resolve short model names.
    77→    if path not in _UNAUTHENTICATED_PASSTHROUGH:
    78→        # Claude Code CLI sends the API key as x-api-key (Anthropic SDK default).
    79→        # Fall back to Authorization: Bearer for other clients.
    80→        session_token = (
    81→            request.headers.get("x-api-key")
    82→            or request.headers.get("authorization", "")[len("Bearer "):]
    83→            or None
    84→        )
    85→        if not session_token or not proxy_token_store.validate_token(session_token):
    86→            raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid or expired session token")
    87→
    88→    headers = {
    89→        k: v for k, v in request.headers.items()
    90→        if k.lower() not in _SKIP_REQUEST_HEADERS
    91→    }
    92→    headers["x-api-key"] = ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
    93→    headers["anthropic-version"] = "2023-06-01"
    94→
    95→    body = await request.body()
    96→
    97→    # Use a fresh client per request: streaming responses that are cut short
    98→    # (e.g. client disconnects) leave connections in a partial read state, and
    99→    # reusing a shared SSL context across those connections causes
   100→    # SSLV3_ALERT_BAD_RECORD_MAC / record layer failure errors.
   101→    # Query params are intentionally NOT forwarded — Claude Code appends
   102→    # internal params (e.g. ?beta=true) that Anthropic rejects as "extra inputs".
   103→    client = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=httpx.Timeout(300.0))
   104→    try:
   105→        upstream_req = client.build_request(
   106→            method=request.method,
   107→            url=f"{ANTHROPIC_UPSTREAM}/{path}",
   108→            headers=headers,
   109→            content=body,
   110→        )
   111→        upstream_resp = await client.send(upstream_req, stream=True)
   112→
   113→        response_headers = {
   114→            k: v for k, v in upstream_resp.headers.items()
   115→            if k.lower() not in _SKIP_RESPONSE_HEADERS
   116→        }
   117→
   118→        async def body_generator():
   119→            try:
   120→                async for chunk in upstream_resp.aiter_bytes():
   121→                    yield chunk
   122→            finally:
   123→                await upstream_resp.aclose()
   124→                await client.aclose()
   125→
   126→        return StreamingResponse(
   127→            body_generator(),
   128→            status_code=upstream_resp.status_code,
   129→            headers=response_headers,
   130→        )
   131→    except Exception:
   132→        await client.aclose()
   133→        logger.exception("Proxy request to upstream failed: %s %s", request.method, path)
   134→        raise

@@ -0,0 +1,170 @@
+"""
+Claude Gateway: LiteLLM-based translation layer for non-Anthropic models.
+
+Routes non-Anthropic model requests through LiteLLM, translating between
+the Anthropic Messages API format and each provider's native format.
+"""
+
+import json
+import uuid
+
+import litellm
+
+_ANTHROPIC_SHORT_ALIASES = {"haiku", "sonnet", "opus"}
+
+
+def is_anthropic_model(model: str) -> bool:
+    """Return True if model name refers to an Anthropic Claude model."""
+    if not model:
+        return True
+    name = model.lower().strip()
+    if name.startswith("claude-") or name == "claude":
+        return True
+    if name in _ANTHROPIC_SHORT_ALIASES:
+        return True
+    return False
+
+
+def _convert_system_to_openai(system) -> str:
+    if isinstance(system, str):
+        return system
+    if isinstance(system, list):
+        return "\n".join(block.get("text", "") for block in system if block.get("type") == "text")
+    return str(system)
+
+
+def _convert_message_to_openai(msg: dict) -> list[dict]:
+    role = msg.get("role", "user")
+    content = msg.get("content", "")
+
+    if isinstance(content, str):
+        return [{"role": role, "content": content}]
+
+    if isinstance(content, list):
+        tool_results = [b for b in content if b.get("type") == "tool_result"]
+        if tool_results:
+            result_msgs = []
+            for tr in tool_results:
+                tr_content = tr.get("content", "")
+                if isinstance(tr_content, list):
+                    tr_content = "\n".join(
+                        b.get("text", "") for b in tr_content if b.get("type") == "text"
+                    )
+                result_msgs.append({
+                    "role": "tool",
+                    "tool_call_id": tr["tool_use_id"],
+                    "content": str(tr_content),
+                })
+            return result_msgs
+
+        tool_uses = [b for b in content if b.get("type") == "tool_use"]
+        text_blocks = [b for b in content if b.get("type") == "text"]
+        text_content = "\n".join(b.get("text", "") for b in text_blocks) if text_blocks else None
+
+        if tool_uses:
+            openai_msg: dict = {"role": "assistant", "content": text_content}
+            openai_msg["tool_calls"] = [
+                {
+                    "id": tu["id"],
+                    "type": "function",
+                    "function": {
+                        "name": tu["name"],
+                        "arguments": json.dumps(tu["input"]),
+                    },
+                }
+                for tu in tool_uses
+            ]
+            return [openai_msg]
+
+        combined = "\n".join(b.get("text", "") for b in content if b.get("type") == "text")
+        return [{"role": role, "content": combined}]
+
+    return [{"role": role, "content": str(content)}]
+
+
+def translate_request_to_openai(anthropic_body: dict) -> dict:
+    openai_messages: list[dict] = []
+
+    system = anthropic_body.get("system")
+    if system:
+        openai_messages.append({
+            "role": "system",
+            "content": _convert_system_to_openai(system),
+        })
+
+    for msg in anthropic_body.get("messages", []):
+        openai_messages.extend(_convert_message_to_openai(msg))
+
+    result: dict = {
+        "model": anthropic_body["model"],
+        "messages": openai_messages,
+    }
+
+    if "max_tokens" in anthropic_body:
+        result["max_tokens"] = anthropic_body["max_tokens"]
+
+    tools = anthropic_body.get("tools")
+    if tools:
+        result["tools"] = [
+            {
+                "type": "function",
+                "function": {
+                    "name": t["name"],
+                    "description": t.get("description", ""),
+                    "parameters": t.get("input_schema", {}),
+                },
+            }
+            for t in tools
+        ]
+
+    return result
+
+
+_FINISH_REASON_MAP = {
+    "stop": "end_turn",
+    "length": "max_tokens",
+    "tool_calls": "tool_use",
+    "content_filter": "end_turn",
+}
+
+
+def translate_response_to_anthropic(openai_resp: dict, model: str) -> dict:
+    choice = openai_resp["choices"][0]
+    message = choice["message"]
+    finish_reason = choice.get("finish_reason", "stop")
+
+    content_blocks: list[dict] = []
+
+    text = message.get("content")
+    if text:
+        content_blocks.append({"type": "text", "text": text})
+
+    tool_calls = message.get("tool_calls", [])
+    for tc in tool_calls:
+        func = tc["function"]
+        try:
+            input_data = json.loads(func["arguments"])
+        except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
+            input_data = {"raw": func.get("arguments", "")}
+        content_blocks.append({
+            "type": "tool_use",
+            "id": tc["id"],
+            "name": func["name"],
+            "input": input_data,
+        })
+
+    usage = openai_resp.get("usage", {})
+
+    return {
+        "id": f"msg_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:24]}",
+        "type": "message",
+        "role": "assistant",
+        "model": model,
+        "content": content_blocks if content_blocks else [{"type": "text", "text": ""}],
+        "stop_reason": _FINISH_REASON_MAP.get(finish_reason, "end_turn"),
+        "stop_sequence": None,
+        "usage": {
+            "input_tokens": usage.get("prompt_tokens", 0),
+            "output_tokens": usage.get("completion_tokens", 0),
+        },
+    }

Now I have all the information I need for a thorough review. Here is my analysis:

---

## Code Review: Claude Gateway Core Implementation (Tasks 2-4)

**Files reviewed:**
- `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/.claude/worktrees/claude-gateway/backend/app/gateway.py` (170 lines, new file)
- `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/.claude/worktrees/claude-gateway/backend/tests/test_gateway.py` (263 lines, new file)

**Plan reference:** `docs/plans/2026-02-26-claude-gateway-design.md` (commit `78333b7f`)

**Test results:** All 17 tests pass.

---

### What was done well

1. **Clean separation of concerns.** The translation functions are pure (no I/O, no state), making them easy to test and reason about. The `_convert_system_to_openai` and `_convert_message_to_openai` helpers keep `translate_request_to_openai` focused on orchestration rather than content type dispatch.

2. **Defensive handling of malformed tool arguments.** The `try/except` around `json.loads(func["arguments"])` with a `{"raw": ...}` fallback at line 146-148 of `gateway.py` is a practical safety net for real-world OpenAI responses that occasionally return invalid JSON in streaming tool calls that get concatenated.

3. **Correct tool use round-trip.** The assistant message with tool_use blocks correctly translates the `id`, `name`, and serialized `input` to OpenAI's `tool_calls` format, and tool_result blocks correctly map `tool_use_id` to `tool_call_id`. This is the most error-prone part of cross-API translation, and it is handled correctly.

4. **Good test coverage for the happy paths.** The tests cover: model detection for multiple providers, system prompt as string and list, tool definitions, tool use messages with both assistant and tool_result sides, response with text, response with tool calls, finish reason mapping, and malformed JSON recovery.

---

### Plan Alignment

The implementation aligns well with the design document's specification for Tasks 2-4:

- **Task 2 (model detection):** Matches the plan's `is_anthropic_model` spec exactly -- `claude-*`, short aliases `{haiku, sonnet, opus}`, everything else is non-Anthropic.
- **Task 3 (request translation):** Covers system prompt, messages, tools, max_tokens, and the tool_use/tool_result round-trip as specified.
- **Task 4 (response translation):** Covers text blocks, tool_use blocks, stop_reason mapping, and usage token translation as specified.

**One notable plan deviation:** The design document says the module will be ~250 lines. The current implementation is 170 lines, but this is because the non-streaming handler (`litellm.acompletion` call) and streaming handler are not yet in this file -- they are planned for Tasks 5 and 6 respectively. This is a reasonable incremental approach, not a problem.

---

### Issues

#### Critical (must fix)

**None.**

#### Important (should fix)

**1. Unused `import litellm` at line 11 of `gateway.py`.**

The `litellm` module is imported but never referenced anywhere in the current code. The translation functions are pure dict-to-dict transformations that do not use LiteLLM. This import forces the `litellm` package (which is large and has many transitive dependencies) to load on module import, adding startup latency even when only the translation helpers are needed.

This should either be removed now and re-added when Tasks 5/6 introduce `litellm.acompletion()`, or converted to a lazy import inside the future handler function.

```python
# gateway.py line 11 -- remove this line for now:
import litellm  # <-- unused, adds ~2s import overhead
```

**2. `is_anthropic_model("")` returns `True` but `is_anthropic_model(None)` will crash.**

At line 18 of `gateway.py`:
```python
def is_anthropic_model(model: str) -> bool:
    if not model:
        return True
```

The type hint says `str`, but in practice the caller will be extracting `model` from a request body dict via `body.get("model", "")`. If `body.get("model")` returns `None` (key present with null value), then `not model` is `True` and it returns `True` safely. However, the subsequent code path with `model.lower().strip()` would crash if the `not model` guard were ever removed or bypassed. The function signature should either explicitly handle `None` via `model: str | None` or the docstring should note the `None`-safe behavior. This is minor but worth tightening since the design document shows the call site as `body.get("model", "")` which could return `None` if the JSON field is literally `null`.

**3. `content_filter` maps to `end_turn` in `_FINISH_REASON_MAP` (line 128).**

```python
_FINISH_REASON_MAP = {
    ...
    "content_filter": "end_turn",
}
```

Mapping `content_filter` to `end_turn` silently hides content moderation events from the consuming SDK/agent. The Anthropic API does not have a direct equivalent, but returning `end_turn` makes it look like the model naturally stopped, when in fact the provider refused to generate. Consider either logging a warning when this mapping fires, or preserving the signal in some way (e.g., appending a text block that says "[Response filtered by provider]"). At minimum, add a code comment explaining the trade-off.

#### Suggestions (nice to have)

**4. Missing test for `None` model value.**

Add a test to verify `is_anthropic_model(None)` behaves as expected, since request bodies can contain `"model": null`:

```python
def test_none_model_is_anthropic_default():
    # model field could be JSON null
    assert is_anthropic_model(None) is True
```

**5. Missing test for tool_result with list content.**

The code at lines 49-52 of `gateway.py` handles `tool_result` where the `content` field is a list of text blocks:
```python
if isinstance(tr_content, list):
    tr_content = "\n".join(
        b.get("text", "") for b in tr_content if b.get("type") == "text"
    )
```

But no test exercises this branch. A test like this would close the gap:

```python
def test_translate_tool_result_with_list_content():
    anthropic_body = {
        "model": "gpt-4o",
        "max_tokens": 1024,
        "messages": [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": [
                    {
                        "type": "tool_result",
                        "tool_use_id": "tool_xyz",
                        "content": [
                            {"type": "text", "text": "Row 1: OK"},
                            {"type": "text", "text": "Row 2: OK"},
                        ],
                    }
                ],
            }
        ],
    }
    result = translate_request_to_openai(anthropic_body)
    tool_msg = result["messages"][0]
    assert tool_msg["role"] == "tool"
    assert tool_msg["content"] == "Row 1: OK\nRow 2: OK"
```

**6. Missing test for multiple tool calls in a single response.**

The code iterates `tool_calls` with a for loop (line 143: `for tc in tool_calls:`), but the test `test_translate_tool_call_response` only includes a single tool call. A test with 2+ tool calls would verify the iteration behavior.

**7. Missing test for `translate_response_to_anthropic` when `content` is `None` (no text, no tool_calls).**

When `message.get("content")` is `None` and `message.get("tool_calls", [])` is empty, the code falls back to `[{"type": "text", "text": ""}]` at line 163. This is a good fallback, but it is untested.

**8. The `_convert_message_to_openai` function has a subtle ordering assumption.**

At line 44, `tool_results` are checked first. If a message contained both `tool_result` and `tool_use` blocks (which would be malformed but possible), only the tool_results would be processed. This is likely fine in practice, but a comment noting the priority would help future maintainers.

**9. Consider adding a brief docstring to the private helpers.**

`_convert_system_to_openai` and `_convert_message_to_openai` handle non-trivial format translation logic but have no docstrings. Even a one-line summary would improve readability, for example:

```python
def _convert_message_to_openai(msg: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """Convert an Anthropic message dict to a list of OpenAI message dicts."""
```

**10. The `pyproject.toml` test configuration section is missing.**

Looking at the existing test patterns (e.g., `test_proxy.py`, `test_dependencies.py`), the test file follows the project's conventions -- plain `pytest` functions, no fixtures, no async. The test file does not have an `__init__.py` marker though -- however, neither do the other test files seem to need one as pytest discovers them by convention. This is fine.

---

### Summary

The implementation is solid, well-structured, and faithfully implements Tasks 2-4 from the design plan. The pure-function approach to request/response translation is the right architecture -- it keeps translation logic testable and decoupled from the I/O layer that will be added in Tasks 5-6.

The two **Important** items to address before moving forward:
1. Remove the unused `import litellm` (line 11 of `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/.claude/worktrees/claude-gateway/backend/app/gateway.py`) to avoid unnecessary import overhead.
2. Consider tightening the `is_anthropic_model` signature to `model: str | None` or adding a guard comment, since the caller could pass `None`.

The **Suggestion** items -- particularly adding tests for the list-content tool_result branch (#5) and multiple tool calls (#6) -- would strengthen coverage for the most complex and error-prone code paths in the translation layer.

This import forces the `litellm` package (which is large and has many transitive dependencies) to load on module import, adding startup latency even when only the translation helpers are needed.

This should either be removed now and re-added when Tasks 5/6 introduce `litellm.acompletion()`, or converted to a lazy import inside the future handler function.

```python
# gateway.py line 11 -- remove this line for now:
import litellm  # <-- unused, adds ~2s import overhead
```

**2. `is_anthropic_model("")` returns `True` but `is_anthropic_model(None)` will crash.**

At line 18 of `gateway.py`:
```python
def is_anthropic_model(model: str) -> bool:
    if not model:
        return True
```

The type hint says `str`, but in practice the caller will be extracting `model` from a request body dict via `body.get("model", "")`. If `body.get("model")` returns `None` (key present with null value), then `not model` is `True` and it returns `True` safely. However, the subsequent code path with `model.lower().strip()` would crash if the `not model` guard were ever removed or bypassed. The function signature should either explicitly handle `None` via `model: str | None` or the docstring should note the `None`-safe behavior. This is minor but worth tightening since the design document shows the call site as `body.get("model", "")` which could return `None` if the JSON field is literally `null`.

**3. `content_filter` maps to `end_turn` in `_FINISH_REASON_MAP` (line 128).**

```python
_FINISH_REASON_MAP = {
    ...
    "content_filter": "end_turn",
}
```

Mapping `content_filter` to `end_turn` silently hides content moderation events from the consuming SDK/agent. The Anthropic API does not have a direct equivalent, but returning `end_turn` makes it look like the model naturally stopped, when in fact the provider refused to generate. Consider either logging a warning when this mapping fires, or preserving the signal in some way (e.g., appending a text block that says "[Response filtered by provider]"). At minimum, add a code comment explaining the trade-off.

#### Suggestions (nice to have)

**4. Missing test for `None` model value.**

Add a test to verify `is_anthropic_model(None)` behaves as expected, since request bodies can contain `"model": null`:

```python
def test_none_model_is_anthropic_default():
    # model field could be JSON null
    assert is_anthropic_model(None) is True
```

**5. Missing test for tool_result with list content.**

The code at lines 49-52 of `gateway.py` handles `tool_result` where the `content` field is a list of text blocks:
```python
if isinstance(tr_content, list):
    tr_content = "\n".join(
        b.get("text", "") for b in tr_content if b.get("type") == "text"
    )
```

But no test exercises this branch. A test like this would close the gap:

```python
def test_translate_tool_result_with_list_content():
    anthropic_body = {
        "model": "gpt-4o",
        "max_tokens": 1024,
        "messages": [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": [
                    {
                        "type": "tool_result",
                        "tool_use_id": "tool_xyz",
                        "content": [
                            {"type": "text", "text": "Row 1: OK"},
                            {"type": "text", "text": "Row 2: OK"},
                        ],
                    }
                ],
            }
        ],
    }
    result = translate_request_to_openai(anthropic_body)
    tool_msg = result["messages"][0]
    assert tool_msg["role"] == "tool"
    assert tool_msg["content"] == "Row 1: OK\nRow 2: OK"
```

**6. Missing test for multiple tool calls in a single response.**

The code iterates `tool_calls` with a for loop (line 143: `for tc in tool_calls:`), but the test `test_translate_tool_call_response` only includes a single tool call. A test with 2+ tool calls would verify the iteration behavior.

**7. Missing test for `translate_response_to_anthropic` when `content` is `None` (no text, no tool_calls).**

When `message.get("content")` is `None` and `message.get("tool_calls", [])` is empty, the code falls back to `[{"type": "text", "text": ""}]` at line 163. This is a good fallback, but it is untested.

**8. The `_convert_message_to_openai` function has a subtle ordering assumption.**

At line 44, `tool_results` are checked first. If a message contained both `tool_result` and `tool_use` blocks (which would be malformed but possible), only the tool_results would be processed. This is likely fine in practice, but a comment noting the priority would help future maintainers.

**9. Consider adding a brief docstring to the private helpers.**

`_convert_system_to_openai` and `_convert_message_to_openai` handle non-trivial format translation logic but have no docstrings. Even a one-line summary would improve readability, for example:

```python
def _convert_message_to_openai(msg: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """Convert an Anthropic message dict to a list of OpenAI message dicts."""
```

**10. The `pyproject.toml` test configuration section is missing.**

Looking at the existing test patterns (e.g., `test_proxy.py`, `test_dependencies.py`), the test file follows the project's conventions -- plain `pytest` functions, no fixtures, no async. The test file does not have an `__init__.py` marker though -- however, neither do the other test files seem to need one as pytest discovers them by convention. This is fine.

### Summary

The implementation is solid, well-structured, and faithfully implements Tasks 2-4 from the design plan. The pure-function approach to request/response translation is the right architecture -- it keeps translation logic testable and decoupled from the I/O layer that will be added in Tasks 5-6.

The two **Important** items to address before moving forward:
1. Remove the unused `import litellm` (line 11 of `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/.claude/worktrees/claude-gateway/backend/app/gateway.py`) to avoid unnecessary import overhead.
2. Consider tightening the `is_anthropic_model` signature to `model: str | None` or adding a guard comment, since the caller could pass `None`.

The **Suggestion** items -- particularly adding tests for the list-content tool_result branch (#5) and multiple tool calls (#6) -- would strengthen coverage for the most complex and error-prone code paths in the translation layer.

```python
async def _handle_streaming(openai_req: dict, model: str):
    """Handle a streaming request by translating OpenAI SSE chunks to Anthropic format."""
    openai_req["stream"] = True
    openai_req["stream_options"] = {"include_usage": True}
    response_stream = await litellm.acompletion(**openai_req)

    async def generate():
        msg_id = f"msg_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:24]}"
        content_block_idx = 0
        active_tool_calls: dict[int, dict] = {}
        has_emitted_text_block = False
        input_tokens = 0
        output_tokens = 0

        # message_start
        yield _sse(
            "message_start",
            {
                "type": "message_start",
                "message": {
                    "id": msg_id,
                    "type": "message",
                    "role": "assistant",
                    "model": model,
                    "content": [],
                    "stop_reason": None,
                    "stop_sequence": None,
                    "usage": {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0},
                },
            },
        )

        async for chunk in response_stream:
            data = chunk.model_dump()
            choices = data.get("choices", [])

            usage = data.get("usage")
            if usage:
                input_tokens = usage.get("prompt_tokens", 0)
                output_tokens = usage.get("completion_tokens", 0)

            if not choices:
                continue

            delta = choices[0].get("delta", {})
            finish_reason = choices[0].get("finish_reason")

            # Text content
            text = delta.get("content")
            if text:
                if not has_emitted_text_block:
                    yield _sse(
                        "content_block_start",
                        {
                            "type": "content_block_start",
                            "index": content_block_idx,
                            "content_block": {"type": "text", "text": ""},
                        },
                    )
                    has_emitted_text_block = True

                yield _sse(
                    "content_block_delta",
                    {
                        "type": "content_block_delta",
                        "index": content_block_idx,
                        "delta": {"type": "text_delta", "text": text},
                    },
                )

            # Tool calls
            tool_calls = delta.get("tool_calls", [])
            for tc in tool_calls:
                tc_idx = tc.get("index", 0)
                if tc_idx not in active_tool_calls:
                    if has_emitted_text_block:
                        yield _sse(
                            "content_block_stop",
                            {"type": "content_block_stop", "index": content_block_idx},
                        )
                        content_block_idx += 1
                        has_emitted_text_block = False

                    tool_id = tc.get("id", f"tool_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}")
                    func = tc.get("function", {})
                    tool_name = func.get("name", "")
                    active_tool_calls[tc_idx] = {
                        "id": tool_id,
                        "name": tool_name,
                        "block_idx": content_block_idx,
                    }

                    yield _sse(
                        "content_block_start",
                        {
                            "type": "content_block_start",
                            "index": content_block_idx,
                            "content_block": {
                                "type": "tool_use",
                                "id": tool_id,
                                "name": tool_name,
                                "input": {},
                            },
                        },
                    )

                func = tc.get("function", {})
                args_chunk = func.get("arguments", "")
                if args_chunk:
                    yield _sse(
                        "content_block_delta",
                        {
                            "type": "content_block_delta",
                            "index": active_tool_calls[tc_idx]["block_idx"],
                            "delta": {
                                "type": "input_json_delta",
                                "partial_json": args_chunk,
                            },
                        },
                    )

            # Finish
            if finish_reason is not None:
                if has_emitted_text_block:
                    yield _sse(
                        "content_block_stop",
                        {"type": "content_block_stop", "index": content_block_idx},
                    )
                for tc_info in active_tool_calls.values():
                    yield _sse(
                        "content_block_stop",
                        {"type": "content_block_stop", "index": tc_info["block_idx"]},
                    )

                yield _sse(
                    "message_delta",
                    {
                        "type": "message_delta",
                        "delta": {
                            "stop_reason": _FINISH_REASON_MAP.get(finish_reason, "end_turn"),
                            "stop_sequence": None,
                        },
                        "usage": {"output_tokens": output_tokens},
                    },
                )

                yield _sse("message_stop", {"type": "message_stop"})

    return StreamingResponse(generate(), media_type="text/event-stream")


def _sse(event_type: str, data: dict) -> str:
    """Format a Server-Sent Event."""
    return f"event: {event_type}\ndata: {json.dumps(data)}\n\n"
```

    """Handle a streaming request by translating OpenAI SSE chunks to Anthropic format."""
    openai_req["stream"] = True
    openai_req["stream_options"] = {"include_usage": True}
    response_stream = await litellm.acompletion(**openai_req)

    async def generate():
        msg_id = f"msg_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:24]}"
        content_block_idx = 0
        active_tool_calls: dict[int, dict] = {}
        has_emitted_text_block = False
        input_tokens = 0
        output_tokens = 0

        # message_start
        yield _sse(
            "message_start",
            {
                "type": "message_start",
                "message": {
                    "id": msg_id,
                    "type": "message",
                    "role": "assistant",
                    "model": model,
                    "content": [],
                    "stop_reason": None,
                    "stop_sequence": None,
                    "usage": {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0},
                },
            },
        )

        async for chunk in response_stream:
            data = chunk.model_dump()
            choices = data.get("choices", [])

            usage = data.get("usage")
            if usage:
                input_tokens = usage.get("prompt_tokens", 0)
                output_tokens = usage.get("completion_tokens", 0)

            if not choices:
                continue

            delta = choices[0].get("delta", {})
            finish_reason = choices[0].get("finish_reason")

            # Text content
            text = delta.get("content")
            if text:
                if not has_emitted_text_block:
                    yield _sse(
                        "content_block_start",
                        {
                            "type": "content_block_start",
                            "index": content_block_idx,
                            "content_block": {"type": "text", "text": ""},
                        },
                    )
                    has_emitted_text_block = True

                yield _sse(
                    "content_block_delta",
                    {
                        "type": "content_block_delta",
                        "index": content_block_idx,
                        "delta": {"type": "text_delta", "text": text},
                    },
                )

            # Tool calls
            tool_calls = delta.get("tool_calls", [])
            for tc in tool_calls:
                tc_idx = tc.get("index", 0)
                if tc_idx not in active_tool_calls:
                    if has_emitted_text_block:
                        yield _sse(
                            "content_block_stop",
                            {"type": "content_block_stop", "index": content_block_idx},
                        )
                        content_block_idx += 1
                        has_emitted_text_block = False

                    tool_id = tc.get("id", f"tool_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}")
                    func = tc.get("function", {})
                    tool_name = func.get("name", "")
                    active_tool_calls[tc_idx] = {
                        "id": tool_id,
                        "name": tool_name,
                        "block_idx": content_block_idx,
                    }

                    yield _sse(
                        "content_block_start",
                        {
                            "type": "content_block_start",
                            "index": content_block_idx,
                            "content_block": {
                                "type": "tool_use",
                                "id": tool_id,
                                "name": tool_name,
                                "input": {},
                            },
                        },
                    )

                func = tc.get("function", {})
                args_chunk = func.get("arguments", "")
                if args_chunk:
                    yield _sse(
                        "content_block_delta",
                        {
                            "type": "content_block_delta",
                            "index": active_tool_calls[tc_idx]["block_idx"],
                            "delta": {
                                "type": "input_json_delta",
                                "partial_json": args_chunk,
                            },
                        },
                    )

            # Finish
            if finish_reason is not None:
                if has_emitted_text_block:
                    yield _sse(
                        "content_block_stop",
                        {"type": "content_block_stop", "index": content_block_idx},
                    )
                for tc_info in active_tool_calls.values():
                    yield _sse(
                        "content_block_stop",
                        {"type": "content_block_stop", "index": tc_info["block_idx"]},
                    )

                yield _sse(
                    "message_delta",
                    {
                        "type": "message_delta",
                        "delta": {
                            "stop_reason": _FINISH_REASON_MAP.get(finish_reason, "end_turn"),
                            "stop_sequence": None,
                        },
                        "usage": {"output_tokens": output_tokens},
                    },
                )

                yield _sse("message_stop", {"type": "message_stop"})

    return StreamingResponse(generate(), media_type="text/event-stream")


def _sse(event_type: str, data: dict) -> str:
    """Format a Server-Sent Event."""
    return f"event: {event_type}\ndata: {json.dumps(data)}\n\n"

```python
async def _handle_streaming(openai_req: dict, model: str):
    """Handle a streaming request by translating OpenAI SSE chunks to Anthropic format."""
    openai_req["stream"] = True
    openai_req["stream_options"] = {"include_usage": True}
    response_stream = await litellm.acompletion(**openai_req)

    async def generate():
        msg_id = f"msg_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:24]}"
        content_block_idx = 0
        active_tool_calls: dict[int, dict] = {}
        has_emitted_text_block = False
        input_tokens = 0
        output_tokens = 0

        # message_start
        yield _sse(
            "message_start",
            {
                "type": "message_start",
                "message": {
                    "id": msg_id,
                    "type": "message",
                    "role": "assistant",
                    "model": model,
                    "content": [],
                    "stop_reason": None,
                    "stop_sequence": None,
                    "usage": {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0},
                },
            },
        )

        async for chunk in response_stream:
            data = chunk.model_dump()
            choices = data.get("choices", [])

            usage = data.get("usage")
            if usage:
                input_tokens = usage.get("prompt_tokens", 0)
                output_tokens = usage.get("completion_tokens", 0)

            if not choices:
                continue

            delta = choices[0].get("delta", {})
            finish_reason = choices[0].get("finish_reason")

            # Text content
            text = delta.get("content")
            if text:
                if not has_emitted_text_block:
                    yield _sse(
                        "content_block_start",
                        {
                            "type": "content_block_start",
                            "index": content_block_idx,
                            "content_block": {"type": "text", "text": ""},
                        },
                    )
                    has_emitted_text_block = True

                yield _sse(
                    "content_block_delta",
                    {
                        "type": "content_block_delta",
                        "index": content_block_idx,
                        "delta": {"type": "text_delta", "text": text},
                    },
                )

            # Tool calls
            tool_calls = delta.get("tool_calls", [])
            for tc in tool_calls:
                tc_idx = tc.get("index", 0)
                if tc_idx not in active_tool_calls:
                    if has_emitted_text_block:
                        yield _sse(
                            "content_block_stop",
                            {"type": "content_block_stop", "index": content_block_idx},
                        )
                        content_block_idx += 1
                        has_emitted_text_block = False

                    tool_id = tc.get("id", f"tool_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}")
                    func = tc.get("function", {})
                    tool_name = func.get("name", "")
                    active_tool_calls[tc_idx] = {
                        "id": tool_id,
                        "name": tool_name,
                        "block_idx": content_block_idx,
                    }

                    yield _sse(
                        "content_block_start",
                        {
                            "type": "content_block_start",
                            "index": content_block_idx,
                            "content_block": {
                                "type": "tool_use",
                                "id": tool_id,
                                "name": tool_name,
                                "input": {},
                            },
                        },
                    )

                func = tc.get("function", {})
                args_chunk = func.get("arguments", "")
                if args_chunk:
                    yield _sse(
                        "content_block_delta",
                        {
                            "type": "content_block_delta",
                            "index": active_tool_calls[tc_idx]["block_idx"],
                            "delta": {
                                "type": "input_json_delta",
                                "partial_json": args_chunk,
                            },
                        },
                    )

            # Finish
            if finish_reason is not None:
                if has_emitted_text_block:
                    yield _sse(
                        "content_block_stop",
                        {"type": "content_block_stop", "index": content_block_idx},
                    )
                for tc_info in active_tool_calls.values():
                    yield _sse(
                        "content_block_stop",
                        {"type": "content_block_stop", "index": tc_info["block_idx"]},
                    )

                yield _sse(
                    "message_delta",
                    {
                        "type": "message_delta",
                        "delta": {
                            "stop_reason": _FINISH_REASON_MAP.get(finish_reason, "end_turn"),
                            "stop_sequence": None,
                        },
                        "usage": {"output_tokens": output_tokens},
                    },
                )

                yield _sse("message_stop", {"type": "message_stop"})

    return StreamingResponse(generate(), media_type="text/event-stream")


def _sse(event_type: str, data: dict) -> str:
    """Format a Server-Sent Event."""
    return f"event: {event_type}\ndata: {json.dumps(data)}\n\n"
```
